q: 1. Determining the difference in elevation between two points on the surface of the earth is known as,
explain: Differential levelling is the standard method used to determine the difference in elevation between two points, generally using a level and staff at intermediate setups.

q: 2. The imaginary line passing through the intersection of cross hairs and the optical centre of the objective, is known as
explain: By definition, the line of collimation is the imaginary line joining the intersection of the cross-hairs to the optical centre of the object glass, extended further.

q: 3. The rise and fall method ...............
options: is less accurate than height of instrument method
is not suitable for leveling with tilting levels
provides a check on the reduction of intermediate point levels
quicker and less tedious for large number of intermediate sights
explain: Unlike the HI method, the Rise and Fall method includes a calculation check for every single intermediate sight.

q: 4. "Cross-section" and "Longitudinal sectioning" is ...............
explain: Profile leveling is used to determine the elevations of points along a fixed line (longitudinal) and perpendicular to it (cross-section).

q: 5. An invert is taken when the point is ...............
explain: An invert level reading is taken by holding the staff upside down against the ceiling or soffit of a structure located above the instrument's line of sight.

q: 6. The ratio of the angles subtended at the eye, by the virtual image and the object, is known as telescope's ...............
explain: This is the angular magnification, the ratio of the angle subtended by the image to the angle subtended by the object.

q: 7. When the cross-hairs are not clearly visible ...............
explain: Focusing the eye-piece is specifically done to make the cross-hairs appear distinct and sharp for the observer's vision.

q: 8. A Bench mark is a
options: the last station where the survey closes
explain: A bench mark is fundamentally a fixed point whose elevation (reduced level) above a datum is already known and used as a reference for levelling work.

q: 9. Due to curvature of earth the object
explain: The curvature of the earth causes a distant object/point to appear lower than its true elevation when viewed through a level line of sight, requiring a curvature correction to be added.

q: 10. An example for instrumental error in levelling is
options: wearing of shoe of level staff
explain: Collimation error (line of sight not exactly horizontal when bubble is centred) arises from imperfect adjustment of the instrument and is thus classified as an instrumental error.

q: 11. For high sensitivity of the bubble tube
options: a liquid of low viscosity is used
a liquid of low surface tension is used
the bubble space should be long
explain: Sensitivity increases with larger radius of curvature, lower viscosity, lower surface tension, and a longer bubble.

q: 12. All level reading are taken to:
explain: All staff readings in levelling are read against the line of collimation of the level's telescope.

q: 13. During leveling the readings are generally taken by the level man. The staff man also takes the reading if the staff is a type of
explain: On a target staff, the level man directs the staff man to move a target until it aligns with the crosshairs, and then the staff man reads the value.

q: 14. A number of readings taken between back sight and fore sight are called
explain: These are technically called Intermediate Sights (IS). Since 'middle sight' isn't standard terminology, 'none of the above' is selected.

q: 15. A relatively fixed point of known elevation above datum is called
explain: A Bench Mark (BM) is a permanent point of reference whose elevation with respect to a specific datum is known and used for leveling operations.

q: 16. The absence of spherical aberration in a telescope is known as
explain: Aplanatism (or aplanation) refers to a lens system that is free from both spherical aberration and coma.

q: 17. Reading of the metric levelling staff can be taken accurately up to
explain: A metric levelling staff, graduated to 5 mm divisions, can be read accurately to about 0.01 m (10 mm) by estimation between graduations, or precisely to the smallest graduation.

q: 18. A level tube is used to make line of sight horizontal. It is filled with
explain: Liquids like ether, alcohol, or chloroform are used because they have low viscosity and low freezing points, allowing the bubble to move quickly and freely.

q: 19. Dumpy level is used when
options: number of observation to be taken are large from one level position
number of observation to be taken are small from one level position
fly levelling is to be done
explain: Because the telescope is fixed to its supports, the Dumpy level is sturdy and efficient for taking many readings from a single setup.

q: 20. Automatic level has advantages of
options: freedom from errors and external influence
comfortable and has large range of application
explain: Automatic levels use a compensator to maintain a horizontal line of sight, making them faster, more precise, and more reliable than manual levels.

q: 21. The height of instrument method is
explain: The HI (Height of Instrument) method requires fewer calculations per point than the Rise and Fall method, making it faster for large numbers of intermediate sights.

q: 22. The observed reading on a levelling staff was 3.545 m. If the staff was 0.150 m off from the original ground level, what should be correct reading?
explain: If the staff is held 0.150m away/down from the original point, the reading must be adjusted by subtraction (3.545 - 0.150 = 3.395m) to reflect the correct ground position.

q: 23. At a change point .............
options: the first reading was taken from the preceding station
the second reading is taken on the staff from the following station
explain: A change point (CP) requires a Fore Sight (FS) from the old instrument position and a Back Sight (BS) from the new instrument position on the same staff location.

q: 24. Levelling across a river is done by
explain: Reciprocal leveling is specifically designed for situations where a large distance (like a river) prevents the level from being placed in the center.

q: 25. A method of differential leveling is used in order to find the difference in elevation between points when .............
options: the difference in elevation between them is too great
explain: Differential leveling (fly leveling) is employed when points are far apart, obstructed, or have a large elevation difference requiring multiple setups.

q: 26. The collimation method for obtaining the reduced levels of points does not provide a check on
explain: In the collimation (height of instrument) method, intermediate sight reduced levels are computed directly from the H.I. without any independent arithmetic check, unlike fore sights and back sights.

q: 27. The rise and fall method for obtaining the reduced levels of points provides a check on
explain: The rise and fall method computes the rise/fall between every pair of consecutive readings, so it provides a complete arithmetic check on all readings -- back sights, intermediate sights, and fore sights.

q: 28. In leveling, the correction for combined curvature and refraction (in metres) is equal to .............
explain: The combined correction C = 0.0673 D² accounts for both the earth's curvature and atmospheric refraction.

q: 29. For true difference in elevations between two points A and B, the level must be set up .............
options: at any point between A and B
at the exact midpoint of A and B
explain: Placing the level at the exact midpoint ensures that any instrumental or natural errors are identical for both readings and thus subtract to zero.

q: 30. When the image formed by the objective is not situated in the plane of cross-hairs .............
explain: Parallax occurs when the image does not fall on the plane of the cross-hairs; it is removed by properly focusing the objective and eyepiece.

q: 31. In profile leveling, staff readings on two neighboring pegs 20 m apart are 1.00 and 1.20 respectively. Therefore, the proposed road has a
explain: The difference in level is 1.20 - 1.00 = 0.20 m over a distance of 20 m. The gradient is 0.20/20 = 1/100. Since the reading increased from 1.00 to 1.20, the ground is lower at the second point, indicating a falling gradient.

q: 32. The following readings were taken on a uniformly sloping ground, 0.5, 1.0, 1.5, 2.0, 1.2, 1.7, 2.7. Hence the difference in level between the first and last station is
explain: The difference in level is calculated by the sum of Back Sights minus the sum of Fore Sights. Here, the change in reading sequence (2.0 to 1.2) indicates a change point. (0.5 + 1.2) - (2.0 + 2.7) = 1.7 - 4.7 = -3.00, which represents a 3.00 m fall.

q: 33. In a survey it was recorded that Σrise = 0, then
explain: If there are no 'rises' recorded, every subsequent point must be lower than the previous one, indicating the ground is continuously falling.

q: 34. The following sights are taken on a 'turning point'
explain: A turning point (change point) requires both a foresight (to close the current instrument setup) and a subsequent backsight (from the new instrument position), so both are taken there.

q: 35. A relatively permanent point of reference whose elevation is known as:
explain: As defined earlier, a bench mark is a relatively permanent point of reference whose elevation is already known.

q: 36. The telescope of a dumpy level .............
options: is rigidly fixed to the leveling head
can be tilted in a vertical plane
can be taken out of its supports and reversed
permits interchange of eye piece and object glass
explain: In a dumpy level, the telescope is rigidly fixed to its supports and cannot be rotated about its longitudinal axis or tilted vertically.

q: 37. Parallax may be eliminated by
explain: You must first focus the eyepiece to see the crosshairs clearly, then focus the objective to bring the image onto the crosshair plane.

q: 38. Correction for curvature for a distance of 1 km =
explain: The formula for curvature correction is $C_c = 0.0785 D^2$. For $D=1$ km, $C_c = 0.0785$ meters.

q: 39. An example for instrument error in leveling is
explain: Collimation error occurs when the line of sight is not perfectly horizontal when the bubble is centered, which is a direct flaw in the instrument's adjustment.

q: 40. Permanent adjustments of a level are .............
explain: For a dumpy level, the two permanent adjustments are making the axis of the bubble tube perpendicular to the vertical axis and making the line of collimation parallel to the axis of the bubble tube.

q: 41. The line of collimation method of reduction of levels, does not provide a check on .............
explain: Unlike the Rise and Fall method, the Height of Instrument (Collimation) method does not have a built-in arithmetic check for intermediate sights.

q: 42. The rise and fall method of reduction of levels, provides a check on .............
explain: The Rise and Fall method is more rigorous because it includes a check on the calculation of reduced levels for intermediate sights, unlike the Height of Instrument method.

q: 43. The radius of curvature of the bubble tube is generally kept .............
explain: A large radius (like 100m) is required to make the bubble sensitive to very small changes in inclination.

q: 44. The following sights are taken on the turning point .............
explain: At a change point (CP), a Foresight is taken to determine its elevation, and then a Backsight is taken to continue the leveling from that new height.

q: 45. The tangent to the liquid surface in a level tube, is parallel to the axis of the bubble .............
explain: The axis of the bubble tube is defined as the line tangential to the internal surface at its center point.

q: 46. The sensitiveness of a level tube decreases if .............
options: radius of curvature of its inner surface is increased
diameter of the tube is increased
length of the vapor bubble is increased
both viscosity and surface tension are increased
explain: Increased viscosity and surface tension make the liquid 'sluggish', thereby reducing the sensitivity of the bubble's movement.

q: 47. A staff reading taken on a bench mark or a point known elevation is called .............
explain: Any reading taken on a point of known elevation (like a Bench Mark) to start a leveling run is a Backsight.

q: 48. Level line and horizontal line are .............
explain: A level line is a curved line following the earth's spheroidal surface, while a horizontal line is a straight line tangent to the level line at a specific point.
